cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Backward-integrated, dual-shore manufacturing. The integrated set-up covers the MIM manufacturing process together with in-house secondary processes for MIM components, and vertically integrated finishing technologies including electroless nickel and trivalent chromium plating, vacuum and sealed quench heat-treating, precision grinding and CNC machining to micron tolerances. In-house capabilities extend upstream to mold designing and tooling (45 to 50 new tools produced per month) and downstream to plastic injection and insert molding, product assembly and integration services, so the Company offers end-to-end solutions from mold design through finished, surface-treated components. As part of its backward integration strategy the Company has initiated manufacturing of stainless-steel powder and is in the process of establishing an iron powder manufacturing facility at Gowribidanur Industrial Area, Chikkaballapur, Karnataka, targeted by end of Fiscal 2027; it states it will continue developing backward integration capabilities to provide more material options to customers (over 80 alloying options as of March 31, 2026). Manufacturing is dual-shore across India, the United States, the United Kingdom and Mexico across five technologies (metal injection molding, ceramic injection molding, investment casting, precision machining and metal 3D printing), with facilities described as fungible across sectors. On the inbound side there is no integration: all raw materials (metal powders such as carbonyl iron and stainless steel, and polymers including polypropylene, wax and stearic acid) are imported and procured on a purchase-order basis with no long-term supply contracts; imports were 60.95%, 61.80% and 59.63% of total raw material purchases in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, and the top 10 suppliers accounted for 42.91%, 29.55% and 44.68% of total raw material purchase cost. Cost of materials consumed was 20.87%, 17.52% and 15.68% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024. Downstream the Company sells direct to OEMs through three sales offices (China, Germany, United States) and 13 sales representatives across nine other countries.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Top 10 customers contributed 38.41%/38.94%/42.00% of revenue from operations in FY2026/FY2025/FY2024; loss of a top customer could materially affect business and results of operations
- Customer arrangements are typically open/discreet purchase orders without binding volume commitments; customers provide only rolling forecasts/indicative schedules, creating demand-visibility risk
- Revenue from operations outside India was 77.20%/89.92%/88.26% of revenue from operations in FY2026/FY2025/FY2024, exposing the company to FX, geopolitical and trade-policy risk
- Industry/market data (including the 6.8% market-share and largest-manufacturer claims) is drawn from the F&S Report, which was commissioned and paid for by the Company itself; reliance on it for investment decisions is subject to inherent risk
- Certain corporate records relating to the Company's 2001 name change, including allotments and transfers of Equity Shares in the past, are not traceable

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Utilise Fresh Issue net proceeds towards repayment/prepayment, in full or part, of certain outstanding borrowings of the Company.**
- **Set up INDO Flex Precision Private Limited, a JV with AUFLEX Co. Ltd, for specialised production and sale of foldable hinge modules in India and other locations.**
- **Produce 45 to 50 new tools per month, among the fastest in the MIM industry for new product introductions.**
- **Maintain position as the largest global manufacturer of MIM precision components with ~7% MIM revenue market share.**
- **May undertake a Pre-IPO Placement of up to INR 2,000 million (not exceeding 20% of the Fresh Issue), which would reduce the Fresh Issue accordingly.**
- **Net Proceeds of the Fresh Issue (Gross Proceeds ₹5,000 million) to be utilised for repayment/prepayment of outstanding borrowings and general corporate purposes.**
- **Setting up a joint venture, INDO Flex Precision Private Limited, with AUFLEX Co. Ltd (South Korea) to produce and sell foldable hinge modules in India and other locations.**
- **New subsidiary INDO-MIM Arms Components Private Limited incorporated to carry out manufacturing of engineering metal parts.**
- **Maintain global market leadership in MIM technology precision engineering components.**
- **Sustain the ability to produce 45 to 50 new tools per month, positioning the company among the fastest in the MIM industry for new product introductions.**
- **Top 10 customers' share of revenue from operations has been declining (42.00% in FY2024 to 38.41% in FY2026); management flags continued dependence on top customers as a risk to monitor.**
